details:
Explorer 1 is an interactive educational platform that transforms the exploration of abandoned space equipment into an engaging learning adventure for children.

The platform allows children to explore abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars through interactive maps and discover the stories behind each machine. When a child selects a piece of equipment, they are introduced to its mission, purpose, and scientific contributions through simplified storytelling, visual content, and interactive activities.

A friendly companion character named Bob guides children throughout their journey, making the experience more enjoyable and easier to follow. The platform also includes educational quizzes and interactive challenges to encourage curiosity and reinforce learning.

At the end of the learning journey, we plan to add an interactive simulation game that allows children to experience a mission inspired by real space rover missions and apply what they have learned in a fun and practical way. This will help them experience space exploration rather than simply learning about it.

Our project uses NASA information and resources to ensure that the educational content is based on real space missions and scientific discoveries. We used Replit and AI-assisted development tools to build the web-based platform and develop its interactive experience.

What makes Explorer 1 creative is its storytelling approach: instead of presenting abandoned equipment as forgotten objects, we give each machine a story and allow children to discover its importance through exploration.

We considered the target audience’s age, ease of use, scientific accuracy, accessibility, and engagement when designing the platform.

Our goal is to make space knowledge more accessible to young learners, inspire curiosity about space exploration, and preserve the stories of machines that contributed to humanity’s understanding of the Moon and Mars.
